title: Another Leg Up In US Inflation?
gist: US headline CPI rose to 3.7% y/y in September from 3.4% in August, driven by elevated energy prices. Gavekal's base case is that long-term inflation expectations stay anchored while the rise is energy-supply-driven, and that rising real borrowing costs, widening high-yield spreads and CoreWeave's -15% plunge signal financial strains that could make the inflation spike short-lived.
